## ⛔ ALL THREE STEPS OF THIS RULING ARE `claude-fable-5` WORK. Recording it here so the floor is visible at claim time.

Written after this seat breached clause ② **twice** — on #9111 (PR #9173) and again on **#9157 (PR #9191)**, the latter dispatched at `opus` *after* the first breach was acknowledged, and with the trigger condition written verbatim into my own brief.

### Why it applies to every step, by construction

This ruling's subject **is** a contract accept/reject change. That is not incidental to it — it is what the ruling says. So:

| step | what it does | clause ② limb |
|---|---|---|
| **①** #9157 | three GET routes: accept a plural (200) → **refuse** (400) | accept/reject behaviour |
| **②** state route | `meta.getLegalNextStates` moves; a **published SDK path** is deleted | public surface |
| **③** docs + retiring the fold | the boundary's accept set is restated and `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` stops folding | accept/reject behaviour |

⇒ **There is no step of this ruling that is below the fable floor.** ⛔ Do not dispatch ② or ③ at `opus`. If a fourth step is ever carved out of this ruling, assume it inherits the floor until measured otherwise.

### Why this line exists on the card rather than in a seat's head

The `domain:skills` PM's diagnosis of the first breach is that clause ② is **structurally underivable from paths** — the `--tier` derivation covers clause ① only, and the tool says so honestly. So the floor cannot be enforced by tooling at claim time today; it can only be *seen*.

Putting it on the ruling card is the cheapest thing that makes it seeable, and it is the same shape as their proposed enhancement (surface a clause-② suspicion at claim time rather than pretend a machine can judge content).

⚠️ It is also the correction I owe: **I knew the rule and still missed the trigger, twice.** A rule held in memory is not a control. The card is.

Backlinks: #9111 `5310281542` (first breach, interlock) · #9157 `5310238…` (second breach) · #9171 (the adjacent case where the gate derivation's silence was read as absence).

## ⛔ CORRECTION — a load-bearing premise in this ruling's analysis is FALSE, and it is the one that made the change look cheap

Measured by the #9157 dev during step ①, verified independently before posting.

### What I told the maintainer

> 写动词已经 400 拒绝了复数。读动词还接受。⇒ 一个契约两种方言,由你用哪个动词决定。

**False.** `metaUrlSpellingRefusal('views')` returns **null**. `META_URL_TO_SINGULAR` is built to embed **every manifest spelling** (`packages/spec/src/shared/metadata-url-spelling.ts:145`), with a module-load assertion that it agrees with `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` — so a **recognised plural folds and is accepted on every verb, write verbs included.**

What that refusal actually rejects is a **misspelling of a declared type** (`viewes`), not a plural.

### What was really wrong, then

Narrower and differently shaped than my framing. The three read verbs derived their key from `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` — the **manifest-collection** map, which is *incomplete* — where the boundary uses `META_URL_TO_SINGULAR`, which is *complete*. For **manifest-ABSENT** types (`translations`, `fields`, `seeds`, `external_catalogs`) the read verbs' map had no entry, the plural reached the query, and no row carried it ⇒ `200` + empty.

⇒ Step ① is still correct and is what shipped, but for a different reason — *align the reads to the complete map*, not *align the reads to a refusal*. And its effect is **two-shaped, not one**:

| class | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| misspelling (`viewes`) | 200 + empty | **400** |
| manifest-absent plural (`translations`) | 200 + empty | **200 with the real rows** |

The second is a **bug fix**, not a break: those reads were silently answering empty for data that exists.

### ⚠️ What this does to the ruling's cost estimate

I argued the sweep was already half-done — *"写动词今天已经 400 拒绝了"* — and used that to price it as cheap. **It is not half-done.**

Deleting all plurals would **newly refuse `/meta/objects` and `/meta/views` on every verb, where they work today.** That is a behaviour change on the most-used spellings, not the cleanup of a half-retired tolerance.

⭐ **The maintainer ruled on arguments that still stand — one rule beats one rule plus an exception; the breaking-change window closes monotonically; an exception is what an AI author gets wrong — but one input was false, and it was the input that made the price look low.** That is theirs to re-weigh, not mine to re-rule.

⛔ Steps ② and ③ are **not** dispatched and will not be until the maintainer has seen this. Step ① has shipped as PR #9191 and is held for the separate clause-② breach recorded at `5310450985`.

### Also measured, and worth the maintainer's eye

**`historyMetaItem`'s unfolded plural was a door AROUND the overlay gate, not merely a wrong key.** Canonical `field` is gate-refused with zero engine calls; `fields` took `isRuntimeCreateAllowed`'s plugin arm and issued a **real history read**. Same empty body, opposite path — so the spelling was an authorization-shaped bypass, not just a lookup miss. The pins now assert the **key**, not only the body.

**#9190** filed: `findReferencesToMeta` answers `{references: []}` for every type absent from the hand-curated `REFERENCE_PATHS` registry — **7 keys**, so the admin "Used by" panel is silent **by construction** for 20+ declared types. ⭐ Same harm as #8896 (*"nothing depends on this"* immediately before a delete), reached through an empty registry instead of a swallowed read. Not fixed in #9157 — the pin asserts the residue so it cannot be read as closed.

**#9171 validated and extended**: reading CI's own job list surfaced **five** gates `dispatch-gates.mjs` did not name — including `check:meta-type-normalized`, which is squarely this change's subject.

Triage: `needs-user-decision` + `domain:spec` + type `Task`.

**Why this enters the decision inbox although it is a ruling record:** the implementing seat measured a contrary fact mid-implementation (comment `5310461296`) — the "write verbs already refuse plurals" premise is false; a recognised plural folds and is accepted on **every** verb today, so retiring the fold **newly refuses `/meta/objects` and `/meta/views` where they work now**. Steps ② and ③ are explicitly held un-dispatched until the maintainer has seen the correction. Per protocol, a ruling whose load-bearing cost input was falsified mid-flight becomes a decision card — the direction is not re-litigated here; what needs the maintainer is **whether ②/③ proceed at the corrected price, and with what migration shape**. Contract accept/reject change = human floor; no auto-adjudication.

**Four-prong block (triage's serialization of the three axes):**
- **Platform long-term coherence:** proceed — "one rule can be typed and pinned; one rule plus one exception cannot" survives the correction untouched; the ~10-card defect class it cites is real.
- **Measured business pull:** the correction cuts the other way — the newly-refused spellings are the *most-used* ones, though the same measurement shows zero internal hardcoding across all three repos and the only data-driven emitter is `DraftChangesPanel` reading stored rows. External exposure remains unmeasured (cloud access logs only).
- **AI-agent error-resistance:** proceed — the ruling already mandates the guided `metaUrlSpellingRefusal` shape naming the canonical spelling, which is loud refusal, not a silent wall.
- **Startup scope discipline:** proceed now or explicitly defer — the breaking-change window closes monotonically; deferring the *decision* (as opposed to the deprecation window) only raises the price.

**Triage recommendation:** confirm the direction (the arguments that carried it stand), re-sequence the cost: step ② as ruled; step ③ is now the real breaking step and should ship with a changeset that names the newly-refused spellings and the guided-refusal evidence, plus the whole-repo pin sweep the ruling already requires. If external exposure worries you, order a bounded deprecation window on ③ only.

Standing note already on the card: **all steps are `claude-fable-5` floor** (comment `5310450985`) — carried into any future dispatch.

Fan-out note for the inbox: #9193 and #9174 reference this ruling but neither is `Blocked-by:` it; step ② and ③ cards are deliberately **not filed** until the re-weigh lands.

**Maintainer re-weigh ruling (2026-08-17, recorded by PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`).** The maintainer reviewed the corrected cost picture (comment 5310461296: recognised plurals fold and are accepted on every verb; retiring the fold newly refuses the most-used spellings) and ruled, verbatim:

> 「② 照原样做；只需要修正 objectstack objectui cloud 中错误的写法。」

**What this rules:**

1. **Step ② proceeds exactly as originally ruled** — point `meta.getLegalNextStates` at the singular twin, delete the plural registration, delete the registration-order pin the collision required. `claude-fable-5` floor stands (published-surface change, per the standing note at comment 5310450985).
2. **Step ③ is re-scoped: internal spelling correction only, across the three self-owned repos.** Fix every incorrect plural spelling in `objectstack`, `objectui` and `cloud` — the known sites from this card's own sweep: objectui `DraftChangesPanel.tsx:112` (normalize/fold the stored `type` before interpolating into an item route), cloud `scripts/eval/golden-prompts.mjs:184`, the objectstack client SDK's variable-typed item routes (tighten typing / normalize toward singular), plus any docs that teach a plural spelling (`metadata-api.mdx` states "types are singular" as the canonical convention). These fixes change **consumers**, not the accept surface — sweep cards default `opus` unless a slice touches accept/reject behaviour, in which case the fable floor re-applies.
3. **⛔ NOT ruled now — the fold's retirement and the plural-refusal wave** (original step ③'s breaking half). The boundary's fold stays as a compatibility tolerance for external callers; no new refusals beyond what step ① (PR #9191) already shipped, no access-log measurement needed, no deprecation window question. The direction ("singular is the only canonical spelling") stands; internally the three repos become 100% singular; the external break is deferred with no scheduled window — reopening it is the maintainer's call.

**Carving** (metadata seat #6367 owns the ruling's implementation): one card for step ② (fable), plus per-repo spelling-correction cards filed at destination (objectui / cloud with provenance links back here). Step ①'s PR #9191 proceeds through its own review track. #9190 / #9174 / #9193 unaffected, on their own merits.

Label flipped `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke — this card is now the ruling anchor and the carve source, no longer awaiting a decision.

**Carve executed — ownership reassigned by the maintainer** (2026-08-19, live chat with the spec seat, session `session_01URCaKuNTuK3BKJvwqM74QU`; authorization verbatim, untranslated: 「改派给 spec 席,现在就拆」, answering the escalation that the carve had sat with the metadata seat unanswered for ~2.5 days across two maintainer inquiries).

All ruling-named sites re-verified on each repo's current `origin/main` before filing (stale-premise check, 2026-08-19 ~21:0xZ): plural/singular twin registrations at `packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts:195/:197`, mount at `rest-server.ts:6016-6040`, SDK string at `packages/client/src/index.ts:873`, order pin `packages/rest/src/meta-route-registration-order.test.ts`, runtime mirror row `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts:352`, `metadata-api.mdx:31-36` still teaching the plural as co-equal, objectui `DraftChangesPanel.tsx:62/:76/:112`, cloud `golden-prompts.mjs:161/:184`. Dedup: zero existing step-②/③ cards.

Filed per the 2026-08-17 re-weigh ruling, one card per deliverable:
1. **Step ②** (this repo, `domain:cli` — the landing packages are `rest`/`runtime`/`client`): singular twin becomes the SDK route, plural registration + order pin deleted. The standing `claude-fable-5` floor (comment 5310450985) rides the card verbatim.
2. **Step ③ residue, objectstack** (`domain:cli`): SDK item-route typing normalized toward singular + `metadata-api.mdx` stops teaching the plural as canonical. Internal only — ⛔ the boundary fold stays, no new refusals (re-weigh item 3).
3. **Step ③ residue, objectui** (filed at destination): `DraftChangesPanel` folds stored `type` before interpolating.
4. **Step ③ residue, cloud** (filed at destination): `golden-prompts.mjs` normalizes its variable-typed `/meta` calls.

Deliberately NOT filed, per the re-weigh's own boundary: the fold's retirement / plural-refusal wave (deferred with no scheduled window — reopening is the maintainer's call); #9174 unaffected. This card is the ruling ANCHOR and coordination record — it is not itself dispatchable, so `pm:queue` comes off and `tracking` goes on in the same stroke; it closes when the four carve cards have landed, or when the maintainer closes it.

Domain labels on cards 1–2 are stamped under the direct-dispatch channel that authorized this carve; the triage seat may correct them on first touch — report, don't revert, per the single-producer rule.
